title: Valuation comparison from semistable to stable modifications
statement: Let $V$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$ [def-weil-field], meaning that $V\subseteq K$ and for every $a\in K^\times$ at least one of $a,a^{-1}$ lies in $V$. Assume its height is finite, meaning its prime ideals form a finite chain. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $(C,D)$ be a multipointed $S$-curve with smooth generic curve and etale generic marking. Suppose $f:(C_{\mathrm{st}},D_{\mathrm{st}})\to(C,D)$ is a stable $\eta$-modification and $g:(C^{\prime},D^{\prime})\to(C,D)$ is a semistable $\eta$-modification. There exists a morphism of pairs $h:(C^{\prime},D^{\prime})\to(C_{\mathrm{st}},D_{\mathrm{st}})$ with $fh=g$, inducing $f_\eta^{-1}g_\eta$ on the generic pair. No assumption that $K$ is separably closed or that $V$ is discrete is imposed. A multipointed curve $(X,D)$ over a scheme $T$ means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms $X\to T$, $D\to T$ of pure relative dimensions $1$, $0$ and a closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; $D$ may be empty and $X$ need not be separated or proper over $T$. It is semistable if every singular point of every geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, $D\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $D$ lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For integral $T$ with generic point $\eta$, an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves is a compatible pair $f_X:X'\to X$, $f_D:D'\to D$ of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism], each an isomorphism over a schematically dense open and on its generic fibre. A semistable such modification is stable if in each geometric fibre there is no irreducible component isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ that is contracted by $f_X$ and meets the union of the marking and the singular points of $X'$ in at most two points. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the local completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\Omega[[u,v]]$ denotes the two-variable formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Here an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective.

proof.text: First assume $K$ separably closed. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-common-strict-semistable-refinement] to the two given $\eta$-modifications $f,g$. It supplies a common strictly semistable (hence semistable) pair $(W,E)$ and $\eta$-modifications $a:(W,E)\to(C_{\mathrm{st}},D_{\mathrm{st}})$ and $b:(W,E)\to(C^{\prime},D^{\prime})$ with $fa=gb$. The lemma requires no semistability of the base pair and no separatedness or properness over $S$.

source.place: Proposition 4.5.1 final paragraph and Remark 4.5.2, printed p. 33.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-valuation-contracted-component-inclusion] to $a,b,f,g$. For every $s\in S$, any irreducible component of $W_s$ contracted by $b_s$ is contracted by $a_s$. All its hypotheses hold: $W$ and $C^{\prime}$ are semistable, $f$ is stable, and every generic map is the specified isomorphism. The conclusion is fibre-component data, not yet a factorization.

source.place: Corollary 4.4.3(i), first sentence of its proof, printed p. 31.

proof.text: The valuation ring $V$ is integrally closed: if $x\in K\setminus V$ were integral, then $x^{-1}$ would be in the maximal ideal of $V$, and multiplying a monic equation by $x^{-n}$ would give $1$ in that ideal. Thus $S$ is normal. By [lem-trf-geometrically-reduced-eta-normal], the semistable curve $C^{\prime}$ is reduced and $\eta$-normal. The other curves are reduced by the same lemma or flatness with smooth generic fibre. The component inclusion of Step 2 and [lem-trf-valuation-component-factorization] give a $C$-morphism $h:C^{\prime}\to C_{\mathrm{st}}$ with $hb=a$ and the required generic map. To obtain the marking map, pull back the ideal of the closed subscheme $D_{\mathrm{st}}$ along $h|_{D^{\prime}}$. Every local section of its image vanishes on the generic fibre. Apply [lem-sc-flat-invertible-sections-torsion-free] on affine opens of the flat $V$-scheme $D^{\prime}$ with the invertible module $\mathcal O$: sections inject into their localizations at $V\setminus\{0\}$, so the image ideal is zero. The closed-immersion factorization therefore gives $D^{\prime}\to D_{\mathrm{st}}$. It lies over $D$ because both composites into $C$ agree and $D\hookrightarrow C$ is a monomorphism. This proves the separably closed case, including an empty marking.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3, printed p. 27, and Corollary 4.4.3(i); marking factorization by the flatness/torsion-free argument.

proof.text: For arbitrary $K$, choose $V^s\subset K^s$ by [lem-trf-valuation-separable-closure-extension]. Pull back $f,g$ to $S^s=\operatorname{Spec}V^s$. They are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. They retain their isomorphisms on the generic fibre and on the pulled-back common open. That open stays schematically dense: on affine charts the defining injective map into sections on the open stays injective after the flat extension $V\to V^s$ (compute sections with a finite affine cover of the quasi-compact open). By [lem-trf-semistable-marked-base-change], all multipointed, semistable and geometric stability conditions persist. The extension maps generic point to generic point, so generic smoothness and etaleness persist as well. Steps 1--3 over the finite-height ring $V^s$, whose fraction field is separably closed, give a comparison of pairs $h^s$.

source.place: Proposition 4.5.1 after valuation extension; flat base change and geometric stability, with the arbitrary-field descent argument made explicit.

proof.text: Put $B=V^s\otimes_V V^s$. The two pullbacks of $h^s$ agree after localizing $B$ at $V\setminus\{0\}$, since there both are the fixed map $f_\eta^{-1}g_\eta$. They are maps over $C_B$ into $C_{\mathrm{st},B}$, whose morphism to $C_B$ is proper and hence separated, by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Their equalizer is consequently a closed subscheme of $C^{\prime}_B$. Its defining ideal vanishes after the stated localization. Since $B$ is flat over $V$, $C^{\prime}_B$ is flat over the original domain $V$. By [lem-sc-flat-invertible-sections-torsion-free] with $L=\mathcal O$, on every affine open its sections have no $V$-torsion. Thus the equalizer ideal is zero and the curve maps agree. Exactly the same argument for the flat marking $D^{\prime}_B$ and separated map $D_{\mathrm{st},B}\to D_B$ gives equality of marking maps. This proves the cocycle condition over $B$ directly; no claim that $B$ is a valuation ring is used.

source.place: Flat generic-fibre uniqueness argument; properness gives the closed relative diagonal.

proof.text: The base-change maps $C^{\prime}_{S^s}\to C^{\prime}$ and $D^{\prime}_{S^s}\to D^{\prime}$ are fpqc covers. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] separately with targets $C_{\mathrm{st}}$ and $D_{\mathrm{st}}$. Step 5 supplies precisely the equality on their double overlaps. The descended maps commute with the marking immersions and satisfy $fh=g$, since their composites do so on these covers and the uniqueness clause of the same descent lemma reflects equality. The generic restriction is $f_\eta^{-1}g_\eta$: on the generic fibre $f_\eta$ is an isomorphism and $f_\eta h_\eta=g_\eta$. This gives the asserted morphism of pairs over $V$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_semistable_to_stable_valuation_comparison (K : Type u) [Field K] (V : ValuationSubring K) [Finite (PrimeSpectrum V)] (P Pst P' : MultipointedCurve (Spec (.of V))) (hXη : Smooth (pullback.snd P.x (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.subtype)))) (hDη : Etale (pullback.snd P.d (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.subtype)))) (f : MultipointedCurve.Hom Pst P) (g : MultipointedCurve.Hom P' P) (hf : f.IsStable (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.subtype))) (hg : g.IsEtaModification (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.subtype))) (hsemistable : P'.IsSemistable) : ∃ h : MultipointedCurve.Hom P' Pst, h.curve ≫ f.curve = g.curve ∧ h.marking ≫ f.marking = g.marking ∧ h.curveBaseChange (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.subtype)) = g.curveBaseChange (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.subtype)) ≫ @inv Scheme.{u} _ _ _ (f.curveBaseChange (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.subtype))) hf.1.2.2.2.2.1 ∧ h.markingBaseChange (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.subtype)) = g.markingBaseChange (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.subtype)) ≫ @inv Scheme.{u} _ _ _ (f.markingBaseChange (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom V.subtype))) hf.1.2.2.2.2.2
